title: Paraintelligence agents
summary: Building government agents who hunt the supernatural.

claims.text: Agents are built with Attributes 6/4/3, Abilities 11/7/4, three Background dots, Willpower 3 and 21 freebie points, which can buy Numina, Merits and Flaws.
Every paraintelligence agent must take at least one dot each of Firearms, Investigation and Occult, and also receives Allies 3, Influence 2 and Resources 2.
A player chooses the agent’s agency, such as the FBI, the NSA or the CIA, and a faction within it, or plays a double agent.
Silver bullets are neither hard nor costly to make, but few agents carry them.
Many paraintelligence divisions still treat silver against werewolves as a theory, and department heads fear embarrassing questions if police or press discovered such rounds.
Agents may requisition them only when the facts of a case justify it.
The Special Affairs Department is thought to date from the end of the Truman years, but its roots go back to the 1930s.
Its founder, Charles Horner, was a young federal agent working Chicago gangland cases with Eliot Ness when a vampire attacked and left Horner for dead.
Horner survived and from then on pursued every case that hinted at the supernatural.

title: The NSA
summary: The National Security Agency and the supernatural.

claims.text: The NSA was founded in secret in the winter of 1952 by a seven-page order from President Truman whose contents have never been made public.
Built from the Armed Forces Security Agency and other services, it has become the most powerful and secretive intelligence agency in the world, with little congressional oversight.
Its Domestic Intelligence Bureau was compromised by supernatural powers.

title: The Garou dilemma
summary: Why werewolves have little hold on human institutions.

claims.text: Compared with vampires and mages, werewolves hold the weakest grip on humanity’s ruling institutions.
Mighty as individuals, they are nearly powerless as a social force, and few show interest in taking hold of government, industry, religion or the media.
Instead they wage an increasingly desperate rearguard war against the advance of Wyrm and Weaver that comes with human progress.
